title: Field-coefficient compact support is triangulated and preserves lower bounds
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of quasi-separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For $\Lambda=E$ use the rationalized category $D^b_c(-,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and for $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ use the common finite-stage category $D^b_c(-,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], equipped with the standard bounded t-structures of [prop-constructible-truncations]. The compact-support functor of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] is an exact functor of triangulated categories
$$Rf_!:D^b_c(X,\Lambda)\longrightarrow D^b_c(Y,\Lambda).$$
For every $c\in\mathbf Z$ and $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$,
$$\bigl(\mathcal H^i(K)=0\text{ for all }i<c\bigr)\ \Longrightarrow\ \bigl(\mathcal H^i(Rf_!K)=0\text{ for all }i<c\bigr).$$
Exactness here includes a natural comparison $Rf_!(K[r])\simeq(Rf_!K)[r]$ compatible with distinguished triangles. No separatedness of $X$ or $Y$ over $k$ is assumed.

Finite-coefficient model: Stacks Tag 0G2A, more-etale.tex, lemma-derived-lower-shriek-bounded, part (3).

proof.text: Fix a compactification $c=(j,p)$ at every coefficient level. The exact $\mathcal O_E$-linear strict coefficient-tower functor [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor], followed by the exact total derived inverse limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], defines the integral functor $F_E^{\rm int}$, including its natural shift maps, triangles and morphisms. Its object formula is [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], and [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible] puts its values in the integral constructible category. By [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound], choose $e$ bounding the dimensions of the fibres $X_y$ of $f$ ($Y$ is quasi-compact). A geometric fibre over $\bar y\to y$ is the base change of $X_y$ along $\kappa(y)\to\kappa(\bar y)$, with the same local dimensions at points over each other by [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change]; its dimension, the supremum of its local dimensions, is therefore also at most $e$. The finite-level exact triangulated functors have the uniform bound $[a,b]\mapsto[a,b+2e]$ by [prop-finite-compact-support-constructibility]; in particular they preserve the lower bound of any bounded finite-coefficient complex.

proof.text:
We identify this tower construction with the completed-coefficient compactification composite used in the scalar-coherence theorem below. Write $K_n=K\otimes^L A_{E,n}$. Derived completeness gives $K\simeq R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_nK_n$ [def-weil-derived-complete]. By [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction], reduction is computed by the two-term complex $[B\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}B]$. The exact, termwise functor $j_!$ of [det-sf-open-closed-extension-zero-limits] commutes with this two-term cone, including its quotient-induced transition maps; restriction of coefficient actions does not change the underlying extension-by-zero sheaf. That same node (2) gives preservation of sequential derived limits. Thus $j_!K\simeq R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_nj_!K_n$. Apply [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison] to the proper map $p$ and the complete object $j_!K$: it gives the canonical comparison
$$Rp_*j_!K\simeq R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRp_{*,n}j_!K_n,$$
with the specified quotient projections and transition maps. The finite-level identifications in [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars] identify these terms with $\operatorname{Res}_nR p_{*,n}j_!K_n$ and commute with successive reductions. Hence this is exactly the prescribed $F_E^{\rm int}K$, naturally in $K$ and compatibly with shifts. For the category domains, finite-type schemes over $k$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] (a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), and finite-dimensional by [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] applied to their structure maps. The same holds for the proper finite-type compactification. The equivalence of the integral conventions here and the compatible PBC integral category is stated in [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. Thus these are the actual completed-category functors, on the same domains.

proof.text: The rational categories of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] are raw scalar localizations of the integral categories, with the same objects. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] to the exact $\mathcal O_E$-linear integral functor from Step 1. It gives an exact $E$-linear functor $F_E$ with the localized natural shift comparison. Explicitly it sends a rational morphism $u/\varpi^m$ to $F_E^{\rm int}(u)/\varpi^m$. On objects it is precisely the rational compact-support formula of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Step 2 identifies it with the rationalization of $Rp_*j_!$. This proves both triangle preservation and the natural shift comparison at every finite field stage, including their compatibility on rational morphisms.

proof.text:
The two coefficient presentations must be compared before descent. [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] identifies the completed integral category used by PBC with the derived-complete integral category used in [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. For $E\subset L$, [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] gives a natural isomorphism $\chi_{L/E,K}$ from ordinary completed derived scalar extension to strict quotient-tower scalar extension. After rationalization, its inverse is a natural comparison
$$j_{Y,L/E}:J_{Y,L}T^{\rm sf}_{L/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}T^{\rm pbc}_{L/E}J_{Y,E},$$
where $J_{Y,E}$ is the identity on integral objects and localized Hom groups. The $L=E$ clause gives the unit equation; naturality of $\chi$, [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition], and the associator and shift equations in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] give the successive-extension, associator, and shift equations for $j$. The common-stage arrow and cone formulas of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] and [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones] therefore yield an exact equivalence $J_Y$ from the framework category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] to the PBC pair category [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], by conjugating each common-stage arrow by the relevant $j$. Apply [lem-cbc-rational-compact-support-coefficient-coherence] to the identity base-change square $X'=X$, $Y'=Y$, $g'=1_X$, $g=1_Y$, with compactification $c'=c$. Its hypotheses hold: Step 2 gives Noetherian, finite-dimensional, separated finite type, and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ is invertible. [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] therefore gives an exact PBC common-stage functor. Transporting it by $J_X$ and $J_Y^{-1}$ gives the required exact functor on [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]; on $(E,K)$ it is $(E,F_EK)$, with arrows given by the $j$-conjugated formula.

proof.text: Let $H$ be an integral constructible sheaf placed in degree zero. Clause (iii) of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] gives a finite stratification on which $H$ is pro-etale locally $B_X\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}N_s$ for a finitely presented $\mathcal O_E$-module $N_s$. The valuation ring is a DVR, hence a Noetherian PID, by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr](2). By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] the torsion submodule of each $N_s$ has finitely many generators; each generator is killed by a power of $\varpi$, so their maximum kills that torsion submodule. Take the maximum over the finitely many strata. Flatness of the completed coefficient sheaf over the constant ring [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] identifies the kernels of multiplication by $\varpi^n$ with the base changes of $N_s[\varpi^n]$. The same local description, finite generation of submodules, and the Noetherian quotient argument show that both $T_n=H[\varpi^n]$ and $H/\varpi^nH$ are constructible finite-coefficient sheaves. Therefore one exponent $N\geq1$ kills all sheaves $H[\varpi^n]$, for every $n$. This bound comes from the constructible cohomology models, not from a finite-module inverse-limit criterion.

source.place: Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); clause (iii) of the integral characterization

proof.text: The two-term free resolution $[B_X\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}B_X]$ of $(A_{E,n})_X$ is valid by [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction]. It computes $H_n=H\otimes^L A_{E,n}$ with cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$, namely $T_n=H[\varpi^n]$ and $H/\varpi^nH$. By Step 5's local-model argument and [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], these two sheaves are constructible; the truncation triangle below therefore lies in the finite constructible category. The quotient $A_{E,n+1}\to A_{E,n}$ lifts to the map of these resolutions which is multiplication by $\varpi$ in degree $-1$ and identity in degree $0$: $\varpi^n\varpi=\varpi^{n+1}$. Hence the transition $T_{n+1}\to T_n$ is multiplication by $\varpi$. Apply the canonical truncation triangle $T_n[1]\to H_n\to(H/\varpi^nH)[0]\to$ of [lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle]. The finite-level exactness and lower interval bound supplied by [prop-finite-compact-support-constructibility], together with the integral output comparison [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible], show for $L_n=\operatorname{Res}_nRf_{!,n}H_n$ that $\mathcal H^q(L_n)=0$ for $q<-1$ and $\mathcal H^{-1}(L_n)=\operatorname{Res}_n\mathcal H^0(Rf_{!,n}T_n)$. These identifications are natural for quotient-induced transitions. Indeed [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars] identifies the finite-level functors across coefficient restriction, so truncation naturality identifies the transition with the map induced by $T_{n+1}\to T_n$. The composite from $n+N$ to $n$ is induced by $\varpi^N:T_{n+N}\to T_n$, which is zero by Step 5. Thus the degree $-1$ cohomology tower of $L_n$ is pro-zero.

source.place: Tag 0G2A, lemma-derived-lower-shriek-bounded (3), and the explicit two-term resolution computation

proof.text: Use the sheaf-valued Milnor sequence [det-pe-milnor-sequence] for $L=F_E^{\rm int}H=R\lim_nL_n$ on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, with its completed ring sheaf; the equality with the defining compact-support tower is [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. For $q<-1$ both adjacent cohomology towers in that sequence are zero by Step 6, so $\mathcal H^q(L)=0$. For $q=-1$ its left term is $R^1\lim\mathcal H^{-2}(L_n)=0$ and its right term is $\lim\mathcal H^{-1}(L_n)=0$: any compatible family has $n$-th component equal to its image from $n+N$, and that transition is zero. Consequently $\mathcal H^{-1}(L)=0$ integrally, not merely torsion. We have proved $F_E^{\rm int}H\in D^{\ge0}$ for every integral heart object.

source.place: Clause (1), the natural Milnor sequence of pro-etale module sheaves

proof.text: The schemes $X,Y$ are Noetherian, finite-dimensional, with $\ell$ invertible (Steps 2 and 4), and [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] identifies their integral categories, completed ring sheaf and cohomology sheaves with those of [prop-weil-localized-tstructure]; so its rational categories are those of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and its $\mathcal C_E^{\ge0}$ is the class of [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure](2). Every rational heart object is isomorphic to $QH$ for an integral heart object $H$, by the heart assertion of [prop-weil-localized-tstructure]. Its t-exact localization functor sends the conclusion of Step 7 into the rational $D^{\ge0}$; Step 3 identifies this image with $F_E(QH)$. This proves the rational heart lower bound. For a common-stage heart object represented by $(E,K)$, [prop-constructible-truncations] says that cohomology and truncation commute with finite scalar extension and with the common-stage construction. Since the object is its own zeroth cohomology, it is isomorphic to the image of the rational heart object $\mathcal H^0(K)$. Its compact-support image is therefore represented by the rational $F_E\mathcal H^0(K)$, which is in $D^{\ge0}$. The common-stage $D^{\ge0}$ is the isomorphism closure of such stagewise objects by [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure](3). This proves the heart lower bound over $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ using the actual functor of Step 4.

source.place: Propositions 6.8.11(3) and 6.8.14, with the stated localized/common-stage standard t-structure comparisons

proof.text: For arbitrary $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ with $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for $i<c$, use the bounded canonical truncation triangles $\tau^{\le q-1}K\to\tau^{\le q}K\to\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]\to$ of [prop-constructible-truncations]. Step 8 puts $Rf_!\mathcal H^q(K)$ in $D^{\ge0}$; the natural shift comparisons of Steps 3–4 put the image of the $q$-th heart layer in $D^{\ge q}$. Starting from $\tau^{\le c-1}K=0$, induct through the finite cohomological range. At each step exactness from Steps 3–4 gives the image triangle, and the long exact sequence of t-structure cohomology in [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](5) implies that the image of $\tau^{\le q}K$ has no cohomology below $c$. At the top truncation this is $K$, which proves the asserted lower bound.
